title: Culture of Leishmania protozoans for lipophosphoglycan extraction and purification
author: Teufel, dos Santos

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare buffers A, B, C and solvent E as described; work in a fume hood, keep containers closed because the buffers are volatile.

steps.title: Pool parasite lysates
steps.instruction: In 15 mL tubes pool lysates, never mixing procyclic with metacyclic promastigotes or different strains; distribute so each tube contains ≈2.5 × 10¹⁰ parasites (≈25 × 10⁹) and adjust buffer volumes proportionally if parasite numbers differ.

steps.title: Pellet lysates
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 5 min at 3000 × g, 21 °C to obtain a pellet.

steps.title: Extract with buffer A
steps.instruction: Perform two successive extractions with buffer A.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 7.5 mL buffer A; stir continuously with a PTFE‑coated magnetic bar and shake vigorously with a glass pipette.
Incubate 5 min at 4 °C, then centrifuge 5 min at 3000 × g, 21 °C.
Discard both the top chloroform layer and the bottom aqueous layer, keeping the pellet; repeat the whole procedure once more.

steps.title: Extract with buffer B
steps.instruction: Perform four successive extractions with buffer B.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 7.5 mL buffer B; shake vigorously with a spatula.
Centrifuge 5 min at 3000 × g, 21 °C and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the resuspension‑centrifugation‑discard cycle three additional times.

steps.title: Extract with buffer C
steps.instruction: Perform three successive extractions with buffer C.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 7.5 mL buffer C; shake vigorously with a glass pipette ensuring homogeneous mixing (as in buffer A).
Centrifuge 5 min at 3000 × g, 21 °C.
Decant the top and bottom layers together, leaving the loose pellet in the tube; repeat two more times.

steps.title: Extract with solvent E
steps.instruction: Perform four successive extractions with solvent E and collect supernatants.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 7.5 mL solvent E; shake vigorously with a spatula.
Collect the supernatant in a clean glass bottle.
Repeat the resuspension‑collection cycle three more times (total four extractions) and discard the pellet after the fourth extraction.

steps.title: Lyophilize solvent E supernatants
steps.instruction: Transfer the pooled solvent E supernatants to 15 mL Falcon tubes and lyophilize under vacuum to obtain raw LPG.

steps.title: Prepare phenyl‑Sepharose columns
steps.instruction: Set up Sephadex G‑15 columns with phenyl‑Sepharose and equilibrate with buffer L.

substeps.instruction: Add 5.5 mL phenyl‑Sepharose to each column using a syringe without drying the resin; tap to remove bubbles.
Equilibrate the column three times with 6 mL buffer L per equilibration (total 18 mL), using a syringe and avoiding air bubbles.
Dry the column just above the resin layer by gently adding air with the syringe.
Note: columns can be stored in 25‑30 % EtOH at 4 °C for reuse after proper washing and equilibration.

steps.title: Resuspend raw LPG in buffer L
steps.instruction: Dissolve the lyophilized LPG in buffer L at 2 mL per column; flush collection tubes to recover all LPG and pool the fractions.

steps.title: Load LPG onto column
steps.instruction: Apply the LPG suspension to the prepared column.

substeps.instruction: Flush the sample tube with 1 mL buffer L.
Add the LPG suspension (wash fraction) onto the column.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer L
steps.instruction: Pass 10 mL buffer L through the column.

steps.title: Wash column with acetic acid
steps.instruction: Pass 4 mL of 0.1 M acetic acid through the column.

steps.title: Wash column with Milli‑Q water
steps.instruction: Pass 4 mL Milli‑Q water through the column.

steps.title: Elute LPG with buffer E
steps.instruction: Elute LPG using buffer E and collect the flow‑through.

substeps.instruction: Pass 10 mL buffer E through the column.
Collect the eluate in a clean glass bottle.
Weigh the container before and after freeze‑drying to determine the mass of isolated LPG.

steps.title: Evaporate volatile solvents
steps.instruction: Dry the eluate under a gentle stream of nitrogen or argon to remove ethanol and diethyl ether before freeze‑drying.

steps.title: Lyophilize purified LPG
steps.instruction: Lyophilize the dried sample under vacuum in 15 mL Falcon tubes to obtain purified LPG.

steps.title: Resuspend LPG for protein assay
steps.instruction: Dissolve the purified LPG in PBS containing 0.5 % DMSO and determine protein concentration with a BCA assay.

steps.title: Store purified LPG
steps.instruction: Aliquot and store the LPG at –20 °C; avoid freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Optional TLC analysis
steps.instruction: Perform thin‑layer chromatography to verify presence of sugars in the LPG preparation.

substeps.instruction: Inactivate a TLC plate by running it in 10 mL of 5 % triethylamine in dichloromethane; dry under N₂ or vacuum.
Spot the sample (≈5 µL) 1 cm from the bottom edge; apply five successive drops on the same spot, allowing it to dry between applications.
Develop the plate in TLC eluent (depth <1 cm) until the solvent front reaches ~90 % of the plate height.
Dry the plate, then dip it into 10 % sulfuric acid in methanol (acid added to methanol on ice) to stain.
Char the plate with a heat‑gun; LPG appears as a faint brown spot against the white silica background.

description: Leishmaniasis is a collective term for several tropical diseases caused by protozoans of the species Leishmania. Clinical manifestations in humans range from localized self-healing skin lesions to chronic disease which affect large areas of the skin, mucosa, and/or inner organs. Disease outcome largely depends on the infecting Leishmania species and/or strain as well as on host-factors. Although millions of infections occur annually, treatment options are still suboptimal, also because they differ depending on the infecting species and the immunological status of the host, and no vaccine is available.2 Some Leishmania surface antigens possess immunogenic properties which promote disease establishment, mediate immune invasion, and thus contribute to disease progression. These antigens, such as the macromolecule LPG, are highly species-, strain-, and life cycle-specific.3 Therefore, they can be used to aid a fast diagnosis to choose the correct treatment regimen. However, they could also be exploited for vaccine development or antigen-specific immunotherapy approaches. Symptoms of therapy-unresponsive patients with cutaneous leishmaniasis and diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis have been successfully treated with immunotherapy combining the tuberculosis vaccine Bacillus Calmette-Guérin with heat-killed L. amazonensis promastigotes or with standard therapy and lysates of L. amazonensis and L. braziliensis promastigotes.4,5 Moreover, we have investigated the highly immunogenic LPG of L. braziliensis as inducer of trained immunity with potent anti-cancer properties in mice.1 In-depth, structural characterization of LPG is therefore an important step in improving healthcare for this tropical, neglected disease. The protocol presented below describes specifically the extraction of metacyclic L. braziliensis LPG from clinical isolates maintained as laboratory culture.
